economic rationale: Easier financing conditions — lower rates and spreads, calmer markets, a weaker currency — support valuations and risk appetite with a lag.
construction: (FCI_t − FCI_t−6) ÷ expanding sd of that 6M change (≥36 obs); FCI oriented so higher = easier
data source: GSFCI (US), BFCIEU (EZ), GSGBFCI (UK), GSEAFCI (CH — euro-area), GSJPFCI (JP)

economic rationale: Analysts revise forecasts gradually, so upgrades persist and prices under-react to them.
data source: Monthly_EPS (US), BEst EPS (EZ, UK, CH, JP)

economic rationale: The forward earnings yield relative to the local risk-free alternative measures how much an investor is paid to hold equities; judged against each market's own history rather than against structurally different peers.
construction: (100 / forward P/E − 2Y government yield), expanding within-country z (≥36 obs)
direction: wider spread vs own history ⇒ more attractive
data source: BEst P/E Ratio and the 2Y government yield for each market

economic rationale: A smooth, directional price path suggests information is being absorbed gradually rather than in shocks; the sign ensures a smooth DECLINE scores negatively.
construction: sign(slope) × R² from a regression of log reconstructed price on a 12-month time trend
data source: Reconstructed index = BEst P/E × forward EPS (see §1a)
